title: HLC receive skew check bypassed when now_ms near u64::MAX
description: TRIGGER: A peer sends an article whose HLC timestamp has wall_ms close to u64::MAX (e.g. wall_ms = u64::MAX - 1), and the local clock now_ms is also near u64::MAX (e.g. system clock rollover or malformed NTP sync). BEHAVIOR: In crates/core/src/hlc.rs, receive checks observed.wall_ms > now_ms.saturating_add(self.max_clock_skew_ms). When now_ms is near u64::MAX, saturating_add clamps to u64::MAX, making the right-hand side u64::MAX regardless of max_clock_skew_ms. Any observed.wall_ms <= u64::MAX passes the skew check, so an arbitrarily far-future timestamp is accepted. This allows a malicious peer to inject a timestamp that makes every subsequent locally generated HLC timestamp larger, permanently inflating the clock and potentially affecting ordering guarantees in the group log.
